title: Ines and the Provision
premise: Ada Zhou, a railroad engineer hiding from a wrongful conviction, survives by mapping abandoned rail lines through the northern monsoon country. When a dying prospector named Ines trades her a map to a flooded provision depot for a promise—deliver it to the daughter she abandoned—Ada is pulled into a journey down closed lines with a leaking boat and a stranger named Ruth who knows too much about Ada's past. Hunted by the railway security chief who framed her, Ada must choose between staying invisible and testifying at last. The story ends with Ada delivering Ines's map, exposing the frame-up using the depot's records, and finding an unexpected family in Ruth and Ines's daughter.
about_author: Petra Kavanagh is a former surveyor's assistant who spent six seasons in remote rail camps before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people the maps forgot.

chapters.title: The Dying Trade
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Working alone on a closed line, Ada finds prospector Ines collapsed beside the tracks. With her last strength, Ines trades a map to a provision depot for a promise: take it to her daughter in Port Merrow. Ada, who trusts no one, accepts only because Ines is dying. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion cracking Ada's isolation.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada studies the map and realizes the depot sits beyond the flood line, reachable only by river during monsoon season. She preps her leaky boat, rationing supplies, while flashbacks reveal her conviction for a bridge collapse she didn't cause. Emotional beat: dread of exposure warring with duty to the dead.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Lock
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At a derelict lock, Ada encounters Ruth, a sharp-tongued salvage diver who recognizes her from wanted notices—and offers help anyway, claiming she owes Ines a debt. Ada can't afford to refuse a second pair of hands. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two secrets circling each other like dogs.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. The storm hits early. They shelter in a signal box where Ruth reveals she once worked for the railway's security chief, Voss—the man who framed Ada—and fled after finding his ledgers. Emotional beat: trust deepens through shared enemies; fear becomes purpose.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The boat springs a serious leak; they lose half their provisions and a cache of Ruth's evidence to the water. Ada blames herself, and old shame surfaces—that she ran instead of fighting her conviction. Emotional beat: rock bottom; Ada nearly turns back.

chapters.title: The Depot
chapters.summary: POV Ada. They reach the provision depot, half-drowned but intact, and find Ines's hidden stores plus something better: shipping manifests proving Voss falsified inspection reports before the bridge collapse. Emotional beat: hope rekindled; the map was never just a map—it was evidence all along.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Voss's patrol boat finds them at the depot. A tense standoff in the flooding warehouse; Ruth stalls him while Ada escapes through a maintenance tunnel with the manifests, taking a bullet graze. Emotional beat: sacrifice and terror; Ada realizes Ruth chose her over safety.

chapters.title: Port Merrow
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Wounded and half-starved, Ada reaches Port Merrow and finds Ines's daughter, Mara—a ferry mechanic who wants nothing to do with the mother who left. Ada gives her the map anyway and tells her how Ines died. Emotional beat: grief and anger; forgiveness neither promised nor refused.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Ada. With Mara's testimony and the salvaged duplicate ledgers Ruth hid separately, Ada walks into the railway tribunal and lays out Voss's fraud publicly as he arrives to arrest her. Voss is taken into custody; Ada's conviction collapses. Emotional beat: climax; justice seized outside the law, then ratified within it.

chapters.title: New Lines
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Weeks later, Ada surveys reopened track with Mara crewing her instrument chain and Ruth running salvage contracts nearby. On the depot's rebuilt shelf, three names are carved side by side. Emotional beat: resolution; invisibility traded willingly for a found family and a future drawn in new lines.
